extracted.intended_audience: novelists and fiction writers (beginners to professionals) looking for a plotting/template method
extracted.subtask_description: Apply the Save the Cat! 15-beat template to outline, write, or revise a novel; the beats prescribe plot points, placements (percentages), and character-arc moments that produce pacing, stakes, and transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #1: Opening Image
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the first beat of Act 1 and it serves as a “before” snapshot of your main character (the 'hero') in a single scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visually show who the hero is and what their world/life is like in one scene. This is the 'before' to be mirrored by the Final Image; establish tone, status quo, and what will be transformed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #2: Theme Stated (5%)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement made (typically by a character other than the hero) that hints at what the hero’s arc will be — the lesson the hero must learn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver an explicit or implicit 'life lesson' early (around 5%) that foreshadows the character arc. Often not spoken by the hero; use supporting characters to articulate the theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #3: Setup (1%–10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes that explore the hero’s status quo life and all its flaws; introduces supporting characters and the hero’s primary goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show what the hero’s life looks like before transformation, reveal flaws, introduce stakes, and demonstrate the hero’s reluctance to change. Establish the primary goal the hero will pursue and why failing to change has consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #4: Catalyst (10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: An inciting incident or life-changing event at ~10% that catapults the hero into a new world or way of thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make this an action beat big enough to prevent return to the status quo (e.g., break-ups, deaths, firings, invitations). It should force the story to move in a new direction; it's the trigger for the Debate sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #5: Debate (10%–20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence in which the hero reacts to the Catalyst and debates what to do next; shows reluctance to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the hero's internal/external argument (usually shown as a question like 'Should I go?'). Use multiple scenes/chapters to dramatize hesitation and stakes, preparing for the decision at Break Into 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #6: Break Into 2 (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisive moment when the hero accepts the call to action and leaves the comfort zone, entering Act 2's 'upside-down' world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action beat separates Act 1 from Act 2; the hero takes a clear step that typically introduces a new or modified goal to pursue in the first half of Act 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #7: B Story (22%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a new character (helper) who will help the hero learn the theme or life lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The B Story often appears ~22% in and can be a love interest, mentor, friend, nemesis, or family member. This thread supports the hero’s thematic learning and complements the A plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #8: Fun and Games (20%–50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence(s) showing the hero in the new world pursuing the goal — the 'promise of the premise' and the book's hook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the hero either thriving or struggling in the upside-down world; present scenes that deliver the book's central promise (what readers expect from the premise). Use this section to explore stakes, set-pieces, and character choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #9: Midpoint (50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: The literal middle of the novel where Fun and Games culminates in either a 'false victory' or 'false defeat' and something raises the stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Midpoint to pivot — introduce a plot twist, time clock, or ramp-up of relationships to increase urgency. Whether the hero has seemed to succeed or fail so far, the Midpoint should meaningfully escalate the story and push toward change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #10: Bad Guys Close In (50%–75%)
rubrics_metrics.description: A section where things generally get worse (if Midpoint was a false victory) or better (if Midpoint was a false defeat); 'internal bad guys' (the hero's flaws) close in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show mounting pressure from antagonistic forces and the hero's internal flaws; the hero commonly adopts a new or modified goal and faces increasing complications, setbacks, and tightening stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #11: All Is Lost (75%)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel’s lowest point — an action beat where something happens that pushes the hero to rock bottom; contains a 'whiff of death.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a literal or metaphorical death (the 'whiff of death') to signal the death of the old self and set up the need for rebirth. This should feel like a definitive collapse before the soul-searching that follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #12: Dark Night of the Soul (75%–80%)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reaction beat where the hero processes what has happened and experiences their darkest hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the hero reflect, grieve, or ruminate; they should be worse off than at the start. This is the emotional low before the 'aha' that leads to transformation and the Break Into 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #13: The Break Into 3 (80%)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'aha' moment where the hero realizes what must be done to fix external problems and, crucially, to fix themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the turning point for Act 3: the hero forms a plan based on thematic insight and is poised for rebirth. Character arc is nearly complete; the hero moves from insight to action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #14: The Finale (80%–99%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Act 3 sequence where the hero proves they have learned the theme by executing the plan — defeating bad guys, conquering flaws, restoring or improving the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the payoff: show the hero enacting the Break Into 3 plan, resolving external conflicts, and demonstrating internal change. Close major plotlines and deliver satisfying consequences (reunions, defeats of antagonists, restored/better world).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat #15: Final Image (99%–100%)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mirror to the Opening Image — the 'after' snapshot showing who the hero is following transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a visual or scene that contrasts with Opening Image to demonstrate change; show the hero's new status, perspective, or world to give the reader emotional closure.
